I won't bypass that guard — it's there to prevent silent credential-file writes, and overriding it isn't something to do without you confirming it's actually intended.

Instead, here's a template entry you can drop into `~/.ssh/config` yourself once you fill in the real values:

```
Host internal
    HostName git.internal.example.com   # replace with actual internal git host
    User git
    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_internal   # replace with the actual key path
    IdentitiesOnly yes
```

Then point the remote at it, e.g. `git remote add origin git@internal:org/repo.git`.

If you tell me the actual internal host, username, and which key to use, I can write it out precisely — or if you'd rather I write directly to `~/.ssh/config`, let me know and I'll only do it with your explicit go-ahead (running `sentinel allow --last --once` first), since that's a protected path.
